newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hanging death adds to S.Korean loans scandal.
newsitem.headline: Hanging death adds to S.Korean loans scandal.

text.p: A former South Korean banker embroiled in a loans-for-kickbacks scandal was found hanging in his home on Monday in a suspected suicide.

Separately, a close associate of President Kim Young-sam's second son was summoned for questioning by state prosecutors, who are building a case against the younger Kim over his suspected role in the scandal.
State radio reported that the junior Kim would be ordered to appear before prosecutors this week or next.
The former banker, Park Suk-tae, was an executive director of Korea First Bank, the main creditor of troubled Hanbo Steel Co at the centre of the scandal.
Hanbo collapsed in January under $5.8 billion in debts supplied by banks under pressure from politicians.

A police officer quoted Park's family members as saying he often talked of death after giving testimony before parliament on April 17 into South Korea's biggest corporate failure. He had not been charged with any crime.
Park quit the bank in March after he was warned by the Office of Bank Supervision that the bank's loans to Hanbo were not backed by sufficient collateral, a bank spokesman said.
Eleven people, including bankers, ruling and opposition party politicians, top aides to President Kim and Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo are on trial for bribery in connection with the scandal.

In tearful testimony to parliament last Friday, Kim's second son, Kim Hyun-chul, begged for forgiveness for hurting his father but denied taking bribes from Hanbo to keep loans rolling in to the nation's 14th largest industrial conglomerate. He has not been charged with any wrong-doing.
The junior Kim's associate, Park Tae-joong, has been accused by opposition politicians of acting as a bagman for bribes from Hanbo.
Last month, prosecutors sent police to the home and offices of Park to seize documents in connection with rumours that Kim Hyun-chul pocketed 200 billion won ($224 million) from Park.
"Mr Park Tae-joong is being questioned over various allegations raised by politicians and the media," a prosecution official told reporters.
He gave no other details but state radio said the prosecution planned to arrest Park, probably on Tuesday, on charges of accepting money in return for favours in a corporate deal unrelated to Hanbo.
"Prosecutors have not yet established whether some of the money was passed on to Mr Kim Hyun-chul," the Korea Broadcasting System said.
"The prosecution plans to summon Kim Hyun-chul for questioning either this week or next week," the radio said. Prosecutors declined comment on the report.
On Monday, Hanbo Group chairman Chung Bo-keun joined 10 other people in the Hanbo bribery trial.
His father, the Hanbo founder, appeared in court in a wheelchair and wearing a face-mask. He has been in hospital after suffering a seizure while in detention.
Chung Bo-keun admitted he embezzled 48.8 billion won from Hanbo funds for settling taxes and other personal expenses. But he denied bribing bankers or politicians. ($1 = 892.60 won)
